title: Grateful Dead Live at Academy of Music on 1972-03-21
lineage: Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat/0 (48k) -> Dat (Sony D8) -> Samplitude Professional v9.11 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with some early hum and mix quirks, but a high‑energy 1972 show highlighted by a smoking “Looks Like Rain” and an epic Play‑In‑The‑Jam.
ai_review.review: This March 21 ‘72 performance captures the Dead in transition – the bar‑room blues of “Cumberland Blues,” “Big Railroad Blues,” and “Truckin’” feel fresh, while the second set erupts into a soaring Play‑In‑The‑Jam that many fans call a monster.  The source is a soundboard tape; listeners note an initial hum, buzz and a front‑heavy Bobby mix, but later mastering work has cleared up much of the imbalance, making the show overall very enjoyable.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for musical performance (many 5‑star comments) outweighs moderate technical complaints about early mix and hum.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early part of the set has noticeable hum, buzz and a Bobby‑forward mix with Jerry’s guitar/voice low; later mastering improves clarity. Overall tape is listenable and clearer than many early‑70s releases.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set opens strong with bar‑room blues and tight playing despite mix issues; the second set builds into a lengthy, exploratory jam (Play‑In‑The‑Jam) before winding down, showing the band’s evolving energy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar tone is praised (especially wah on “Greatest Story”) but early mix buried his vocals and lead; later sections sound more balanced.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly noted for strong bass work and even singing on “Looks Like Rain”; reviewers say "Phil rocks".
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby’s pedal steel and organ are highlighted, though the mix initially puts him too far forward.
band_member_comments.Keys: Ron’s keyboards are present (organ on “Big Railroad Blues”), but some note his energy wanes in the second set.
